sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned HCGP for respondent No.1.
Respondent No.2, who is served in this matter, has remained unrepresented before this Court.

NC: 2024:KHC:45887 3. F.I.R. in Crime No.50/2024 was registered by Nuggehalli Police Station, Hassan, initially for the offences punishable under Section 376AB of IPC and Sections 4, 8 & 21 of the POCSO Act, against petitioner herein and another, on the basis of first information dated 11.04.2024 received from respondent No.2, who is the aunt of the victim girl aged about six years.
During the course of the investigation petitioner herein was arrested on 12.04.2024 and subsequently remanded to judicial custody.
Investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed against him for the aforesaid offences.
4. The bail application filed by the petitioner in SPL.C.No.195/2024 before the jurisdictional Sessions Court was rejected on 09.08.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court.

sentences.text:
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is youngster, aged about 22 years,
having no criminal antecedents.

Even if the charge sheet allegations are presumed to be true the offence punishable NC: 2024:KHC:45887 under Section 376AB IPC and Section 4 of POCSO Act would not get attracted against the petitioner.
Medical records of the victim do not support the aforesaid allegations made against the petitioner.
Investigation in the case is completed.

Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
6.
Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the bail petition and he submits that the victim is minor aged about six years.
The petitioner has committed a heinous offence on the minor victim girl, in the event petitioner is enlarged on bail, he is likely to tamper with the prosecution witnesses.

Accordingly, prays to dismiss the petition.
7.
First information was submitted by respondent No.2 who is aunt of the victim girl, age about six years.

In the first information it is mentioned that on 10.04.2024 at about 4.30 pm, the victim girl came crying to first informant and informed her, when she went to drink water near the shed, the petitioner took her inside the shed and NC: 2024:KHC:45887 gave her some eatables, thereafter he removed her cloths and also removed his cloths and after making her to sleep on ground and he slept on her and tried to insert his private part into the private part of the victim girl.

Immediately,
thereafter, first informant and others gone near the shed and the petitioner who is inside house alleged ran away, thereafter first informant had approached the police, submitted typed first information based on which FIR in crime No.50/2024 was registered against the petitioner and another.
8. The victim was produced before the Doctor in Hassan Institute of Medical Sciences, Hassan, for her medical examination on the very same day.

entities.text: Hassan Institute of Medical Sciences, Hassan
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Medical examination report of the victim girl would go to show that no external injury was found on the body of the victim girl or on her genitals.
The Doctor has made in the medical examination report that the victim girl has stated that the petitioner had tried to have penetrate sexual assault.

Statement the victim girl was recorded under Section 164 NC: 2024:KHC:45887 of Cr.P.C before the Jurisdiction Magistrate on 24.04.2024, even in the said statement the victim girl has stated that the petitioner had tried to insert his private part into her private part.
9. Section 3 of the POCSO Act, defines the word penetrative sexual assault, and Section 7 of the POCSO Act is defines the word sexual assault.
The petitioner has been charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 4 and also offences punishable under Section 8 of the POCSO Act.
Section 4 provides for punishment for penetrative sexual assault and Section 8 provides for punishment for sexual assault.
The question whether the act committed by the petitioner is punishable under Section 4 or 8 of POCSO Act, is subject matter of trial.
10. Undisputedly, the petitioner has no criminal antecedents, he is aged about 22 years, and he is in custody from 12.04.2024.
Trial in case is yet to commence and the prosecution has all together cited 29 charge sheet witnesses in the present case.

Considering the aforesaid NC: 2024:KHC:45887 aspects of the matter, I am of the view that, without expressing any opinion on the merits and demerits of the case, petitioner's prayer for grant of regular bail needs to be answered affirmatively.
